concerns.text: Task T023 mandates calculating centrality for the 'FULL AAL3 atlas (~90 regions)', directly contradicting Plan.md Phase 1 Task 1.3 which explicitly requires using a 'fixed, a priori set of regions (AAL3 indices 1-10)' to avoid bias. This semantic drift violates the plan's bias-control strategy and the specific constraint to use a fixed subset.

Task T026 calculates VIF across the 'FULL SET OF REGIONS' (~90), whereas Plan.md Phase 1 Task 1.6 requires VIF calculation specifically for the 'three specific metrics (degree, betweenness, eigenvector)' of the fixed region set. Calculating VIF on 90 regions invalidates the plan's multicollinearity resolution logic (switching to PCA for the 3-predictor model).

Task T024 aggregates metrics from the 'full set of regional metrics (all available regions)', violating Plan.md Phase 1 Task 1.5 which mandates aggregating the 'mean of fixed regions 1-10'. This changes the definition of the 'global centrality' predictor from the plan's bias-controlled definition to a full-atlas average.

Task T035 describes permuting residuals but fails to explicitly mandate the 're-fitting of the null model with covariates' for every permutation. The Plan.md Phase 3 Task 3.1 explicitly defines Freedman-Lane as permuting residuals of the null model (including motion covariates) and re-fitting. Omitting the re-fit step constitutes a semantic weakening of the statistical validation requirement.

Task T027 decides between 'Global_Centrality' and 'PCA-Adjusted' based on VIF of the full set. However, Plan.md Phase 1 Task 1.6 requires the VIF check to be performed on the fixed 3-metric set (degree, betweenness, eigenvector) to trigger the PCA switch. The task's logic is misaligned with the plan's specific multicollinearity resolution path.
